list: Official 55 trophies — names, descriptions and grades verbatim as PlayStation publishes them (Exophase / PSNProfiles, 2026-11-18). Kind, stage, target and missable-watch fields are this guide's own editorial organisation, reasoned from the official descriptions.
sources: Official name, description & grade: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list, cross-checked on PSNProfiles (trophies/43531). Progress targets: PSNProfiles, where PSN tracks a count. Guide text: original to Leonida Nights, written from the official descriptions.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum unlocks automatically the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing separate to do in the game. Plan backwards from the long counters instead: 250 stunts, 100 WAiNK spots and $250,000 of laundered bills take far longer than the story, so chip at them from Chapter 1 and let the platinum be a formality at the end of Stage 5.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Gone Fishing, the opening mission. It cannot be skipped or failed permanently: play through the prologue, follow the on-screen prompts as the game teaches movement and cover, and the trophy pops on the mission-complete screen. A gentle first cast — take your time and learn the controls here.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 1. Nothing optional gates it — just follow the story markers as the game hands control between the protagonists. One habit worth starting now: grab cash and side income as you pass it, because the spending and laundering trophies in Stage 5 are much easier when the money grind starts early.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2 of the story. The name is printed exactly as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks included. By now the map and activity icons are opening up: clear the chapter, but start sampling one of each activity type whenever you pass one — Master of None only needs a single attempt at each of the nine types.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3. Mid-story is the right moment to begin the collectible sweep in the areas you have already unlocked — meditation spots, card sets and WAiNK locations are all easier to mop up region by region than in one endgame pass. Keep one eye on the counter steppers in this guide as you travel.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the endgame. Stranger strands should all be available by now: if any strand-giver icons are still untouched on your map, clear them in Stage 2 before pushing to the final mission, so the 100% completion counter closes cleanly.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission for the list's story gold. Go in stocked — full armour, snacks and your best loadout — and treat any mid-mission choice screens carefully: the description of Actions Speak Louder ('Choices made (for better or worse)') tells you this game remembers decisions. The trophy pops when the finale resolves.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Like every named-mission trophy on this list it is earned simply by finishing the mission on any difficulty — if a section keeps failing, drop the pace, use cover, and let your partner draw fire rather than restarting the whole run.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions reward preparation: scout the approach the game offers, keep an escape vehicle in mind before the alarm phase, and finish the mission — the trophy is for completion, not for a clean or undetected run.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Play it as it comes in the chapter order — mission trophies like this one are waypoints on the road to the Chapter trophies, and none of them asks for a medal, a time or a no-damage run.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. If the mission involves a public or performance set-piece, expect crowds and cameras rather than a straight firefight — follow the objective markers, keep moving, and the completion trophy is yours at the wrap-up.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown at the airport. Remember this location: the World trophy Catch Me If You Can also happens at VCIA ('Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA'), so while the takedown plays out, note the exits and airside routes — you will want that knowledge later.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. Operations are the list's set-piece missions: expect a heavier combat load than the chapter average, bring armour and a full weapon wheel, and push through to the completion screen — no optional objective is required for the trophy.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% game completion — the second gold and the real final boss of this list. Story, stranger strands, collectibles and activities all feed the percentage, so work the roadmap stages in order and check the in-game completion screen whenever you stall at a stubborn fraction: it names the category that is still short. Leave this for last; most of it completes itself as the other trophies fall.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts — jumps, flips and airtime feats the game credits as you drive. Natural play earns a steady share; farm the rest at ramps, airfields and coastal jumps, and vary the stunt type, because repeating the identical jump in the identical spot is the slowest way to grow the counter. Use the stepper in the guide pane to pace it: 25 stunts a session finishes this in ten sessions.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 250) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once — the list's own starter data counts nine types, from races and the shooting range to fishing, arcade games and drone races. You do not need to win or even finish most of them: one genuine attempt at each type is enough. Sweep the map's activity icons in a single tour and this pops quietly along the way.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 9 activity types) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal all 42 Shooting Range challenges — the toughest silver on the list. Learn each lane's target rhythm before chasing score, replay a lane immediately while its pattern is fresh, and bank the easy golds first so the counter climbs while you practise. Save the hardest lanes for late, when your handling is sharpest; progress is per-challenge and never lost.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 42 challenges) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location — 14 wins, one per course, and second place does not count. Learn each course with a slow sighting run first, then attack it: drone races are won on the racing line through the gates, not on top speed. Tick locations off in the guide pane so no course is flown twice by mistake.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 14 locations) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — the word 'different' is the whole trophy: repeating one easy race 20 times earns nothing. Spread wins across the map and across vehicle classes, start with the shortest circuits, and bring a tuned car to the longer road races. Twenty distinct wins also pays well, which feeds the money trophies in Stage 5.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 20 races) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing challenges are a test of patience over reflexes: match the bait and spot the challenge offers, keep tension steady rather than hauling, and let Cal's early catches set the target weight. If you lose, re-challenge immediately — the trophy only needs one win.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish, at any arcade cabinet in Leonida. Pick the shortest game on the cabinet menu if you are in a hurry — the trophy asks for a completion, not a high score. This also ticks the arcade type off Master of None's nine activity types.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's whole stranger strand, through to his final mission. Strands unlock in sequence — each completed job reveals the next — so if Andy has gone quiet, progress the story or his earlier jobs first. His finale is one of the eight strands counted by the silver Strangers & Freaks trophy.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission by working his stranger strand from its first job to its last. The boat-accident title hints his strand lives on the water — bring a boat-friendly loadout and expect the finale to test it. Counts toward the eight strands needed for Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's stranger strand through its final mission. Keep his icon pinned whenever you cross his region — strands are easy to leave half-done, and only the final mission of each strand earns its trophy. One of the eight strands behind the silver Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight full mission strands for strangers across Leonida. The named finales on this list — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone — are five of them; the counter in the guide pane tracks the rest as you find them. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so finish what you start before opening new strands.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 8 strands) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission by finishing his stranger strand end to end. His supply-and-demand theme suggests delivery and goods runs — keep a fast, durable vehicle ready for his jobs. The finale counts toward the eight strands of Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's stranger strand, final mission included. As with every strand finale, earlier jobs must be cleared in order before the last one appears; if his marker vanishes, sleep or advance the clock and check the map again. One more of the eight strands behind Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida — 18 in all. Spots sit in quiet, scenic places, so work region by region alongside The Goodtime State's exploration and use the stepper to count them off. A spot only registers when you complete the meditation interaction, so stay until the prompt finishes rather than walking away early.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 18 spots) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret sends you after. Unique means one specific creature, not a species count: take Bret's strand to the hunt, track the animal on foot once you are close, and make the shot count — a spooked unique animal can cost you a long wait for it to settle again.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete three full Collectible Card sets. Cards are scattered collectibles, so this is a sweep trophy: finish one set completely before spreading attention across the others, and pair the hunt with exploration — every new area opened for The Goodtime State is another chance to spot a card glinting off the beaten path.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 3 sets) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations — the list's biggest location grind. Treat it as a travelling habit rather than a single farm: trigger it whenever you arrive somewhere new, keep the counter stepper honest, and let exploration carry most of the total. Saving all 100 for the endgame is the classic way this silver outstays its welcome.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 100 locations) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's bite-size objectives, and most complete themselves during ordinary play — driving, combat and exploration all feed the pool. Check the challenge list whenever the counter stalls and deliberately close out the nearly-done ones; fifty arrives far sooner with a little bookkeeping.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 50 challenges) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, raise a 4-star wanted level, then lose it and escape cleanly. Build the stars somewhere with exits — near tunnels, alleys or a vehicle swap — and break line of sight before the search turns into a chase again. Both conditions matter: the partner must be present and the escape must complete.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops back-to-back with your partner, keeping the wanted level alive between all three. Pick a tight cluster of shops, park for a fast exit, and move straight to the next till — if the stars blink out between shops, the chain breaks and the count restarts. This is the mirror image of Hot Together: there you escape the heat, here you must not lose it.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Discovery is about variety, not ownership: get in, or get close enough for the game to register, every new model you meet. Wealthy districts, docks, airfields and rural roads each spawn different traffic, so tour the map's extremes rather than circling one neighbourhood, and let On the Spot's registrations overlap the hunt.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 100 vehicles) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down five enemies inside a single Combat Focus activation. Do not burn Focus on the first pair you meet — wait for a clustered group of five or more, pre-aim at head height, and sweep across the group in one motion. Gang operations and heist alarms are reliable places to find a crowd standing close together.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 5 in one use) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableNote: Watch reason, quoted from the official description: 'Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.' The trophy is tied to one named location — the same VCIA as the story mission VCIA Takedown — so treat any visit there as a chance to attempt it rather than assuming it can be triggered anywhere, any time.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — in plain terms, leave the airport in a way the airport did not plan for you: take a vehicle or aircraft out outside any mission script. You scouted this ground during Hi-Jacked (VCIA Takedown); use that knowledge of the airside layout, grab something that flies or drives fast, and get out.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.missableNote: Watch reason, quoted from the official description: 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos.' Rhinos are military tanks — hardware that usually appears in scripted, high-heat moments rather than parked in free roam — so when a Rhino shows up, engage with it there and then instead of assuming another will be along later.
trophies.guide: The official description is a joke with a clue inside it: Rhinos are tanks, and it gets hot in them. Get into — or up against — a Rhino when the game puts one in front of you, most likely at maximum heat or in a late set-piece, and survive the encounter. Keep explosives in the loadout for the moment it appears.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — the stealth counterpart to the loud robbery trophies. Case the store first, enter quietly, keep the weapon down and the staff calm, and be out before any alarm state flips to detected. If you are spotted, walk away and try another store rather than forcing the run.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape each time — a robbery only counts when you get away with it. Plan the exit before you open the vault: a fast car positioned for the door, a route that breaks line of sight early, and no looting past the point of greed. Five clean escapes, tracked on the stepper, earns the silver.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 5 vaults) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armoured truck and escape with the take. Trucks are tougher than shop tills: block or stop the truck somewhere with cover, deal with its escort quickly, grab the money and vanish before the wanted level builds past managing. One successful truck is all the trophy asks for.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — 52 areas to uncover. Exploration registers as you physically enter each area, so a map that looks visited from the highway may still hide an uncounted corner. Fly or drive a deliberate grid over any fogged regions late in the sweep, and combine the pass with meditation spots, cards and WAiNK locations so no trip is wasted.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 52 areas) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — nine gangs, one operation each. Variety is the requirement: robbing your favourite gang nine times leaves eight boxes unticked. Spread the hits across the map as you unlock new turf, expect armed resistance at every operation, and track the gangs off in the guide pane.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 9 gangs) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.missableNote: Watch reason, quoted from the official description: 'Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.' It describes one small, specific moment in one named place — the kind of quiet interaction that is easy to walk straight past in the opening hours, so do it the first time you are on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — a quiet, missable-feeling moment rather than a challenge. Head to Ocean Beach, find the spot where drinks are served with the ocean in front of you, order the cocktail and let the moment play out. The name ('In The Beginning…', printed with the ellipsis PlayStation publishes) hints it belongs early in your Leonida story.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style: get inside a showroom, take one of its display vehicles, and drive it out through the glass rather than the door. Pick a showroom with a straight run at the window and a road beyond it, and enjoy the most literal trophy description on the list.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — play the bowling activity at that named alley. The name is printed exactly as PlayStation publishes it, curly apostrophe included. Visit the alley, start the activity and complete your throw with a proper follow-through; it also counts as an activity type toward Master of None if you have not bowled yet.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The official description — 'A partnership with mass appeal' — is deliberately cryptic, and this guide will not invent a location it cannot cite. What the words do say: it is a partner moment, something the two protagonists do together that lands with an audience. Keep doing partner content — the paired robberies, escapes and activities of Stage 5 — and this is the trophy that pops when the partnership performs.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableNote: Watch reason, quoted from the official description: 'Choices made (for better or worse).' A game built on choices can close one path when you take another, so read choice screens before committing — especially around the finale — rather than assuming every alternative stays open.
trophies.guide: PSN tracks this one to 500 — the choices you make across the whole game, 'for better or worse'. It is a volume trophy wearing a story costume: play naturally, take the optional conversations and decisions the game offers instead of skipping them, and the counter fills long before the credits. The stepper in the guide pane shows the PSN target so you can see how passive it really is.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 500) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missableNote: Watch reason, quoted from the official description: 'Second time's the charm.' The description only makes sense as fail-first, succeed-second — if you ace the relevant attempt first time, the 'second time' may never happen, so do not reload a failure away the instant something goes wrong once.
trophies.guide: The official description is the whole riddle: 'Second time's the charm.' This is a trophy about failing once and succeeding on the retry — so when an attempt goes wrong, resist the instinct to reload an old save; play the second attempt the game offers you and let it land. Deliberately scuffing one easy, repeatable attempt is the controlled way to set it up.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Another deliberately vague official description — 'What the hell just happened?' — pointing at a strange, unexpected event somewhere in Leonida. This guide cites no location it cannot back: the honest advice is to explore off the story path, linger when the world does something odd, and investigate anomalies instead of driving past them. Weirdness rewards the curious on this list.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock a pedestrian down with a melee drive-by — swing from a moving vehicle and connect. Ride slowly past a busy sidewalk on a bike or in an open vehicle, time the swing as you pass, and keep the speed low: too fast and you will run the target over instead of bowling them, which is a different and unwanted outcome.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts — a quarter of a million through one specific channel, so ordinary spending and earning do not count. Whenever marked bills land in your inventory from robberies and heists, route them to your contacts rather than sitting on them, and track the running total on the stepper; it is the longest money grind on the list.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: $250,000) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — cumulative, and across all of them, so vehicles, weapons, clothing and garages all feed the same pot. Never sell yourself short to save money on this run: buy the good gear, stock up before missions, and let Little Boxes' garage purchases do some of the heavy lifting. It pops mid-shopping-spree for most platinum hunters.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: $100,000) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — eight in all. This is a savings goal more than a search: bank your heist and race income instead of spending it early, then buy the garages in one sweep once the cash is there. Every purchase also counts toward Treat Yo Self's $100,000 of shop spending, so the two trophies pay each other off.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 8 garages) — Guide: original, from the official description.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Make it a reflex: every time you take a new vehicle for Whip It Good's 100 discoveries, register it before you abandon it, and the two counters climb together. Ten registrations is an afternoon's driving if you swap cars often instead of living in one favourite.
trophies.sources: Official data: Exophase · PSNProfiles (PSN target: 10 vehicles) — Guide: original, from the official description.
